# Adjudication Task — Chapter 336

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃336화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|고목나무.
  6|
  7|노인을 보자마자 머릿속에 떠오른 단어였다.
  8|
  9|사방이 천으로 가로막힌 어두운 전각 안, 홀로 우두커니 서 있는 노인의 뒷모습은 마치 생기를 잃은 고목나무 같았다.
 10|
 11|다음 순간, 그가 천천히 돌아서지 않았더라면 나는 그가 이미 바닥에 뿌리를 내렸을 거라 생각했을지도 모르는 일이다.
 12|
 13|“그래…….”
 14|
 15|녹색 광채가 맴도는 두 눈동자.
 16|
 17|노인, 만독수라(萬毒修羅) 당사독은 뱀처럼 쉭쉭거리는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 18|
 19|“서신을 가져왔다고?”
 20|
 21|중년인이 대답했다.
 22|
 23|“맞습니다. 숙부님. 검성 매종학 대협께서 보내신…….”
 24|
 25|“네게 물었더냐?”
 26|
 27|“……!”
 28|
 29|“네가 낄 자리가 아니다. 이만 물러나라.”
 30|
 31|실수를 깨달은 중년인이 묵례를 취하고 전각을 빠져나갔다.
 32|
 33|자신의 조카를 말 몇 마디로 매몰차게 내쫓은 당사독이 가죽 의자에 비스듬히 몸을 기댔다.
 34|
 35|‘노인네 포스 보소.’
 36|
 37|문제는 그게 악역 포스라는 거지.
 38|
 39|첫인상만 보면 정파가 아니라 마교라고 해도 믿을 정도다.
 40|
 41|나는 당사독의 시선에 한 걸음 앞으로 나섰다.
 42|
 43|“태원진가의 진태경이 만독수라 당사독 대협을 뵙습니다.”
 44|
 45|당사독이 알 수 없는 표정으로 대답했다.
 46|
 47|“적 선배가 말년에 제자를 들였다는 이야기는 익히 들어 알고 있다. 태원진가와도 연이 있고.”
 48|
 49|“아, 그러십니까?”
 50|
 51|이건 좋은 징조다.
 52|
 53|턱을 쓰다듬으며 뭔가를 생각하던 당사독이 문득 입을 열었다.
 54|
 55|“이름이…… 그래, 화양검(火魎檢) 진백양. 이제 기억나는군.”
 56|
 57|좋은 징조는 얼어 죽을. 저 이름은 잊을 만하면 튀어나오네.
 58|
 59|대장로가 정말 한때 잘나가기는 했었던 모양이다.
 60|
 61|사실 그럴 만도 한 것이 그는 정마대전에서 혁혁한 전공을 쌓은 절정 고수였다. 그러니 그 속에서 다른 고수들과 교분을 쌓았다는 것도 이상한 일은 아니다.
 62|
 63|‘심지어 화왕도 한두 번 본 적이 있다고 했을 정도니까, 뭐.’
 64|
 65|덕분에 적천강과의 첫 만남에서 사정을 설명하기도 전에 화염신장을 처맞았었지.
 66|
 67|당사독은 물끄러미 나를 바라보며 물었다.
 68|
 69|“진백양이는 요즘 어떻게 지내느냐?”
 70|
 71|“저어, 그게…….”
 72|
 73|나는 말하기에 앞서 주위를 둘러봤다. 갑자기 어디서 독뱀이 튀어나온다거나, 암기가 쏘아질 때 잽싸게 피하기 위해서다.
 74|
 75|“돌아가셨는데요.”
 76|
 77|“뭣이?”
 78|
 79|그래, 이럴 줄 알았어.
 80|
 81|나는 눈을 부릅뜬 당사독을 향해 황급히 말을 이었다.
 82|
 83|“불의의 사고로 그만. 물론 이게 사정이 있는데 약간의 시간만 주시면 아무 오해 없이 말씀드리겠…….”
 84|
 85|“필요 없다.”
 86|
 87|“예?”
 88|
 89|“재수 없는 놈이었지. 주위에서 대협이니, 협객이니 떠받들어 줄 때마다 기분이 더러웠어.”
 90|
 91|“…….”
 92|
 93|“무림인에게 이유 없는 죽음은 없는 법. 죽으면 그뿐이다.”
 94|
 95|일이 쉽게 풀려서 다행이긴 한데, 노인네 인성이 거의 독극물 수준이다. 단지 재수 없었던 놈이 죽어서 잘됐다는 투가 아닌가.
 96|
 97|‘인성이 거의 암천 수준인데.’
 98|
 99|내 마음에 싹트는 의심을 아는지 모르는지, 당사독은 귀찮다는 듯이 손을 내저었다.
100|
101|“죽은 사람 이야기는 그만하고 본론으로 들어가지. 그래, 매종학 대협이 노부에게 서신을 보냈다고?”
102|
103|“예. 직접 보시는 게 빠를 겁니다.”
104|
105|나는 품 안을 더듬는 시늉을 하며 인벤토리에 넣어 둔 검성의 친필 서신을 소환했다.
106|
107|서신을 건네받아 읽어 내려가는 당사독의 미간이 점점 찡그려지더니, 마침내는 분노로 가득 찬 고함이 터져 나왔다.
108|
109|“이런 쳐 죽일 놈들을 보았나!”
110|
111|후우우웅!
112|
113|웅혼한 공력이 실린 외침에 전각 내부가 부르르 몸을 떨었다.
114|
115|녹색 장포를 펄럭이며 분노를 표출하던 당사독이 씹어뱉는 듯한 말투로 물었다.
116|
117|“서신에 적힌 내용이 전부 사실이냐?”
118|
119|“예. 적힌 그대롭니다.”
120|
121|검성의 서신에는 하남에서의 사건들이 일목요연하게 정리되어 있었고, 적천강의 치료를 위해 신의를 찾는 것에 적극 협조해 달라는 부탁이 적혀 있었다.
122|
123|“적 선배의 상태가 그리 위중하다니…….”
124|
125|“안 그래도 신의를 찾기 전에 부탁드리고 싶었던 일이 있습니다.”
126|
127|사천당문은 독과 암기로 이름을 알렸지만, 가문의 일원 하나하나가 뛰어난 의원이기도 했다.
128|
129|그리고…… 그중에서도 정점에 선 한 사람이 있다.
130|
131|나는 당사독을 똑바로 응시하며 물었다.
132|
133|“태상가주님을 뵐 수 있겠습니까.”
134|
135|독왕(毒王) 당사문.
136|
137|정마대전 이전부터 독과 암기에 관한 한 천하제일이라 불렸던 초절정 고수.
138|
139|한 시대를 풍미했던 그는 이십 년 전, 하나뿐인 자식에게 사천당문의 가주위를 승계하고 사라졌다.
140|
141|비로 지금 내 눈앞의 노인, 당사독에게.
142|
143|“신의를 찾으려면 몇 날 며칠이 걸릴지 모릅니다. 그전에 독왕께서 사부님의 상태를 봐 주신다면…….”
144|
145|“그만.”
146|
147|내 말을 가로막은 당사독이 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
148|
149|“불가(不可). 이게 노부의 대답이다.”
150|
151|“……!”
152|
153|생각지도 못한 반응에 순간 가슴이 덜컥 내려앉았다.
154|
155|독왕 당사문이 오랜 세월 모습을 드러내지 않았다고는 해도, 당사독은 분명히 그의 거취를 알고 있다.
156|
157|불가, 허락하지 않겠다는 것은 알면서도 돕지 않겠다는 뜻이다. 나도 모르게 떨리는 목소리가 입술 사이로 흘러나왔다.
158|
159|“어, 어째서입니까?”
160|
161|“말할 수 없다.”
162|
163|“말할 수 없다고요?”
164|
165|“대신 길을 안내해 줄 사람을 몇 붙여 줄 테니 함께 떠나라. 청성과 아미라면 기꺼이 도와줄 것이다.”
166|
167|내가 지금 뭘 들은 거지?
168|
169|이번의 충격은 앞의 것보다 몇 배는 컸다. 지금 당사독이 한 말에는 이번 일에 관해 사천당문이 도움을 주지 않겠다는 뜻이 담겨 있었기 때문이다.
170|
171|아니, 아예 도움을 안 주는 건 아니다.
172|
173|‘청성파과 아미파까지 안내해 줄 길잡이 몇 명.’
174|
175|그게 전부다. 사천당문에서 받을 수 있는 도움은.
176|
177|쇠몽둥이로 얻어맞은 것처럼 뒤통수가 얼얼했다. 가슴 한구석에서 뜨거운 뭔가가 불쑥 솟구친다.
178|
179|“단지 그것뿐입니까?”
180|
181|“더 무슨 도움을 바랐더냐?”
182|
183|“신의를 찾아야 합니다!”
184|
185|“그건 너희의 사정이지, 노부와 본가의 사정은 아니다. 매종학 대협의 서신을 가져왔다고 해도 마찬가지. 이건 부탁이었고 노부는 거절했느니라. 그뿐이다.”
186|
187|말문이 턱 막혔다.
188|
189|당사독의 말이 모두 맞았다. 그에게, 그리고 사천당문에게 있어 이 모든 것들은 의무가 아닌 선택이다.
190|
191|‘그래, 그랬었지.’
192|
193|마음속으로 설마, 설마 했던 사실을 비로소 깨닫자 지독한 실망감과 분노가 치밀어 올랐다.
194|
195|할 말을 잃어버린 그때, 달콤한 과자 냄새와 함께 한 사람이 앞으로 나섰다.
196|
197|“화산파의 청풍이 인사 올립니다.”
198|
199|저런 모습도 있었나.
200|
201|지금껏 본 적 없는 얼굴과 말투로 포권을 취한 청풍이 말을 이었다.
202|
203|“가주님께서 어떤 연유로 거절하시는지는 모르나, 만약 도와주신다면 이 은혜는 결코 잊지 않을게요.”
204|
205|“네가 매종학 대협의 제자라는 사실을 안다. 강호의 은원(恩怨)을 맺을 때는 신중해야 하는 법. 괜한 오지랖 부리지 말고 물러나거라.”
206|
207|“오지랖이 아닌데요.”
208|
209|“그럼 무엇이냐?”
210|
211|청풍이 올곧은 눈빛으로 대답했다.
212|
213|“할아버지께서는 인의(人意)라고 하셨어요.”
214|
215|“……!”
216|
217|청풍을 복잡한 표정으로 바라보던 당사독이 고개를 가로저었다.
218|
219|“매종학 대협께서 직접 찾아와 부탁해도 노부의 대답은 달라지지 않는다.”
220|
221|“하지만…….”
222|
223|청풍과 궁기방, 혁무진이 동시다발적으로 입을 열려던 그 순간, 내가 불쑥 한마디를 내뱉었다.
224|
225|“이유가 뭡니까?”
226|
227|“이유?”
228|
229|“사천당문이 어떤 힘을 지녔는지는 지나가는 똥개 새끼도 압니다. 그런데 도대체 무슨 이유로 거절하시는 겁니까?”
230|
231|“그 이유, 말하기 싫다면 어쩌겠느냐?”
232|
233|“어쩌긴요.”
234|
235|나는 녹색 빛이 어른거리는 당사독의 눈동자를 응시하며 대답했다.
236|
237|“아까 말씀하신 강호의 은원이 저와 사천당문 사이에 이어지는 거죠. 물론 좋은 쪽은 아니라고 말씀드리고 싶네요.”
238|
239|“……허, 이런 겁 없는 놈을 보았나.”
240|
241|“평소에는 누울 자리 보고 발 뻗는데, 이번 경우에는 제가 좀, 많이 급해서요.”
242|
243|앞으로 남은 시간은 길어야 반년 남짓.
244|
245|천하에서 내로라하는 무림 문파와 황실까지 나서도 찾지 못한 신의다.
246|
247|만약 적천강이 제때 치료를 받지 못해 죽는다면. 사천당문의 도움이 없어서 그렇게 된다면…….
248|
249|“그때는 저도 제가 무슨 짓을 할지 모르겠습니다.”
250|
251|말을 끝맺자 전각 안에는 숨 막히는 침묵이 흘렀다.
252|
253|한참이나 아무 말 없이 심유한 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 당사독이 문득 입술을 뗐다.
254|
255|“적 선배가 저리된 것은 유감이다.”
256|
257|“유감이면 도와주시지 그러십니까.”
258|
259|“노부도 그러고 싶다. 허나 어찌하겠느냐. 지금 본가(本家)에 그만한 여력이 없는 것을.”
260|
261|여력이 없다?
262|
263|그 말을 듣는 순간, 여기까지 오면서 봤던 광경이 눈앞을 스쳤다.
264|
265|삼엄하다 못해 살벌하기까지 한 분위기, 쉴 새 없이 뭔가를 만드는 장인들과 끊임없이 어디론가 날라지는 무기들.
266|
267|“도대체…… 무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는 겁니까?”
268|
269|“벌어져?”
270|
271|저벅.
272|
273|당사독이 나를 향해 걸음을 내디뎠다.
274|
275|그가 익힌 독공(毒功)의 영향일까. 어느 때보다 섬뜩하게 빛나는 그의 녹색 눈동자에 서린 것은 분노와 슬픔이었다.
276|
277|“일은 이미 벌어졌다. 이제 남은 것은 본가의 모든 힘을 총동원하여 이 일에 관련된 흉수를 모조리 척살하는 것뿐이다.”
278|
279|이거다. 사천당문이 지금 우리를 도울 수 없는 이유.
280|
281|나 같은 새파란 핏덩이에게 보는 앞에서 도전적인 말을 듣고도 쉽사리 말하지 못했던 그 이유.
282|
283|신의를 찾아 화왕의 목숨을 구하는 것보다 중요하고, 독왕 당사문과의 만남을 단칼에 거절한 이유.
284|
285|“……설마.”
286|
287|그런 기색을 알아차린 것일까.
288|
289|눈을 부릅뜬 나를 바라보던 당사독이 살기 어린 목소리로 말했다.
290|
291|“소식을 들었을 때는 모든 것이 늦은 후였지. 사지가 온전한 곳이 없더군.”
292|
293|의심을 확신으로 바꿔 주는 한 마디.
294|
295|독왕 당사문이 죽었다.
296|
297|
298|
299|* * *
300|
301|
302|
303|“흠.”
304|
305|적당한 키와 둥글둥글한 얼굴. 중년인은 어디서나 볼 수 있을 법한 용모의 소유자였다.
306|
307|캄캄한 동굴 벽에 기대어 자신의 팔뚝을 유심히 살피던 그가 중얼거렸다.
308|
309|“안 되겠군. 독기(毒氣)가 지독해.”
310|

I stared into Tang Sadok’s green eyes.

[P122]
“Then the ties of gratitude and grudges you mentioned will form between me and the Sichuan Tang Clan. And I should warn you—they won’t be the pleasant kind.”

[P123]
“……”

[P124]
“Hah. What a fearless brat.”

[P125]
“Normally, I know better than to pick a fight I can’t win. But this time, I’m in a bit of a hurry. A hell of a hurry.”

[P126]
Jeok Cheongang had half a year left at most.

[P127]
Even the greatest martial sects under heaven and the Imperial Court had failed to find the Divine Physician.

[P128]
If Jeok Cheongang died because he could not receive treatment in time… If he died because the Sichuan Tang Clan had refused to help…

[P129]
“Then I don’t know what I might do.”

[P130]
When I finished speaking, suffocating silence descended upon the pavilion.

[P131]
Tang Sadok studied me for a long time, his gaze deep and unfathomable. At last, his lips parted.

[P132]
“I regret what happened to Senior Jeok.”

[P133]
“If you’re sorry, why not help us?”

[P134]
“This old man would like to. But what can I do? Our family does not have the strength to spare right now.”

[P135]
No strength to spare?

[P136]
The moment I heard those words, the scenes I had witnessed on the way here flashed through my mind.

[P137]
An atmosphere so tense it bordered on murderous. Artisans working without rest. Weapons constantly being carried from one place to another.

[P138]
“What the hell is going on?”

[P139]
“Going on?”

[P140]
*Step.*

[P141]
Tang Sadok took a step toward me.

[P142]
Perhaps it was due to the poison arts he had cultivated, but his green eyes gleamed more eerily than ever. Within them burned anger and grief.

[P143]
“It has already happened. All that remains now is for our family to marshal its full strength and slaughter every last culprit involved.”

[P144]
That was it.

[P145]
That was why the Sichuan Tang Clan could not help us now.

[P146]
That was why Tang Sadok had been so reluctant to explain himself, even after a green brat like me challenged him to his face.

[P147]
That was why this took priority over finding the Divine Physician and saving the Fire King’s life—and why he had flatly refused to let me meet Poison King Tang Taesang.

[P148]
“Don’t tell me…”

[P149]
Perhaps he saw the realization on my face.

[P150]
Tang Sadok met my wide-eyed stare and spoke in a voice thick with killing intent.

[P151]
“By the time we received the news, it was already too late. Not one of his limbs had been left intact.”

[P152]
Those words turned my suspicion into certainty.

[P153]
Poison King Tang Taesang was dead.

[P154]
* * *

[P155]
“Hmm.”

[P156]
The middle-aged man was of average height, with a round face and the sort of ordinary appearance one might see anywhere.

[P157]
Leaning against the wall of a pitch-black cave, he carefully examined his forearm and muttered.

[P158]
“This won’t do. The poison is vicious.”

[P159]
He clicked his tongue softly.

[P160]
He had done everything he could, but the best he had managed was to force all the poison into one arm.

[P161]
“Poison King… Vicious to the end. Even worse than I expected.”

[P162]
Poison King Tang Taesang.

[P163]
The expression on his face when he finally breathed his last was still vivid in the middle-aged man’s mind.

[P164]
But the result left the middle-aged man in a difficult position.

[P165]
He had succeeded in eliminating the Supreme Peak master known as the Poison King, yet failed to accomplish the more important task.

[P166]
*Not that I ever expected it to be easy.*

[P167]
With that thought, the middle-aged man abruptly brought the edge of his hand down on his left forearm.

[P168]
A dazzling flash burst forth, and the severed forearm fell to the ground.

[P169]
*Schhk! Ssssss!*

[P170]
Poison-laden blood splattered across the cave, melting everything it touched. Acrid toxic smoke billowed into the air.

[P171]
The small creatures watching the middle-aged man from hidden crevices died the instant the smoke reached them, never knowing what had happened.

[P172]
*Eek… Eeeek…*

[P173]
Listening to the bats’ dying shrieks, the middle-aged man walked out of the cave and grinned up at the blazing sunlight.

[P174]
It was impossible to believe that smile belonged to a man who had just cut off his own arm.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“This old man would like to. But what can I do? Our family does not have the strength to spare right now.”

[P135]
No strength to spare?

[P136]
The moment I heard those words, the scenes I had witnessed on the way here flashed through my mind.

[P137]
An atmosphere so tense it bordered on murderous. Artisans working without rest. Weapons constantly being carried from one place to another.

[P138]
“What the hell is going on?”

[P139]
“Going on?”

[P140]
*Step.*

[P141]
Tang Sadok took a step toward me.

[P142]
Perhaps it was due to the poison arts he had cultivated, but his green eyes gleamed more eerily than ever. Within them burned anger and grief.

[P143]
“It has already happened. All that remains now is for our family to marshal its full strength and slaughter every last culprit involved.”

[P144]
That was it.

[P145]
That was why the Sichuan Tang Clan could not help us now.

[P146]
That was why Tang Sadok had been so reluctant to explain himself, even after a green brat like me challenged him to his face.

[P147]
That was why this took priority over finding the Divine Physician and saving the Fire King’s life—and why he had flatly refused to let me meet Poison King Tang Taesang.

[P148]
“Don’t tell me…”

[P149]
Perhaps he saw the realization on my face.

[P150]
Tang Sadok met my wide-eyed stare and spoke in a voice thick with killing intent.

[P151]
“By the time we received the news, it was already too late. Not one of his limbs had been left intact.”

[P152]
Those words turned my suspicion into certainty.

[P153]
Poison King Tang Taesang was dead.

[P154]
* * *

[P155]
“Hmm.”

[P156]
The middle-aged man was of average height, with a round face and the sort of ordinary appearance one might see anywhere.

[P157]
Leaning against the wall of a pitch-black cave, he carefully examined his forearm and muttered.

[P158]
“This won’t do. The poison is vicious.”

[P159]
He clicked his tongue softly.

[P160]
He had done everything he could, but the best he had managed was to force all the poison into one arm.

[P161]
“Poison King… Vicious to the end. Even worse than I expected.”

[P162]
Poison King Tang Taesang.

[P163]
The expression on his face when he finally breathed his last was still vivid in the middle-aged man’s mind.

[P164]
But the result left the middle-aged man in a difficult position.

[P165]
He had succeeded in eliminating the Supreme Peak master known as the Poison King, yet failed to accomplish the more important task.

[P166]
*Not that I ever expected it to be easy.*

[P167]
With that thought, the middle-aged man abruptly brought the edge of his hand down on his left forearm.

[P168]
A dazzling flash burst forth, and the severed forearm fell to the ground.

[P169]
*Schhk! Ssssss!*

[P170]
Poison-laden blood splattered across the cave, melting everything it touched. Acrid toxic smoke billowed into the air.

[P171]
The small creatures watching the middle-aged man from hidden crevices died the instant the smoke reached them, never knowing what had happened.

[P172]
*Eek… Eeeek…*

[P173]
Listening to the bats’ dying shrieks, the middle-aged man walked out of the cave and grinned up at the blazing sunlight.

[P174]
It was impossible to believe that smile belonged to a man who had just cut off his own arm.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 336

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃336화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|고목나무.
  6|
  7|노인을 보자마자 머릿속에 떠오른 단어였다.
  8|
  9|사방이 천으로 가로막힌 어두운 전각 안, 홀로 우두커니 서 있는 노인의 뒷모습은 마치 생기를 잃은 고목나무 같았다.
 10|
 11|다음 순간, 그가 천천히 돌아서지 않았더라면 나는 그가 이미 바닥에 뿌리를 내렸을 거라 생각했을지도 모르는 일이다.
 12|
 13|“그래…….”
 14|
 15|녹색 광채가 맴도는 두 눈동자.
 16|
 17|노인, 만독수라(萬毒修羅) 당사독은 뱀처럼 쉭쉭거리는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 18|
 19|“서신을 가져왔다고?”
 20|
 21|중년인이 대답했다.
 22|
 23|“맞습니다. 숙부님. 검성 매종학 대협께서 보내신…….”
 24|
 25|“네게 물었더냐?”
 26|
 27|“……!”
 28|
 29|“네가 낄 자리가 아니다. 이만 물러나라.”
 30|
 31|실수를 깨달은 중년인이 묵례를 취하고 전각을 빠져나갔다.
 32|
 33|자신의 조카를 말 몇 마디로 매몰차게 내쫓은 당사독이 가죽 의자에 비스듬히 몸을 기댔다.
 34|
 35|‘노인네 포스 보소.’
 36|
 37|문제는 그게 악역 포스라는 거지.
 38|
 39|첫인상만 보면 정파가 아니라 마교라고 해도 믿을 정도다.
 40|
 41|나는 당사독의 시선에 한 걸음 앞으로 나섰다.
 42|
 43|“태원진가의 진태경이 만독수라 당사독 대협을 뵙습니다.”
 44|
 45|당사독이 알 수 없는 표정으로 대답했다.
 46|
 47|“적 선배가 말년에 제자를 들였다는 이야기는 익히 들어 알고 있다. 태원진가와도 연이 있고.”
 48|
 49|“아, 그러십니까?”
 50|
 51|이건 좋은 징조다.
 52|
 53|턱을 쓰다듬으며 뭔가를 생각하던 당사독이 문득 입을 열었다.
 54|
 55|“이름이…… 그래, 화양검(火魎檢) 진백양. 이제 기억나는군.”
 56|
 57|좋은 징조는 얼어 죽을. 저 이름은 잊을 만하면 튀어나오네.
 58|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [

"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
